pr_title: Chunk MariaDB and Postgresql data migration to avoid running out of buffer space
pr_body:
TODO

Test with 85+ million states rows

- [x] mysql
- [x] sqlite 
- [x] postgresql 
## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
The original test case was ~50million state rows which turned out to not be enough to hit some limitations.  This change refactors the migration to handle upwards of 85+ million state rows.

- Chunk MariaDB data migration to avoid running out of buffer space
- Limit the post migration cleanup rows (the rest will be cleaned up over time with purge)

This will make the migration a bit slower for MariaDB but since the `innodb_buffer_pool_size` is using the default to 128M and the addon is not tuned to the db size there is a risk of running out of buffer space for large databases

There are no effective changes for sqlite as it even handled 100 million states rows in far less time than either mysql or postgresql.

Trying to get it all done in one transaction to allow rollback was just never going to happen with mariadb & innodb per row locking limits

Going to take a few more hours to get a good test as it takes about 5-6 hours to insert all the data to get to 20GiB of states and another 1-2 to migrate it, and than I need to test sqlite and postgres again as well but those are faster
With the additional guard we can't do a `Using index for skip scan`

MariaDB runs out of heap since its limited to 128M on the post migration task after 60 million rows
`ROLLING BACK 597808 lock struct(s), heap size 119627896, 61063370 row lock(s), undo log entries 30893724`
I think we can solve that by limiting the post migration cleanup to 40 million rows.  They will eventually get purged anyways

I'm happy with the mysql changes. Tested with 86 million state rows.

Now replicating that testing with sqlite

sqlite is good.

Waiting for the postgres data to populate
script has generated 37Million rows. Will take another few hours to get 75 million
postgres migrated with 80million rows successfully but it used too ram.  I think we can reduce that with a similar method
testing complete. doing final checks now
I think this is good to go now. I'm just doing one more round of checks since its a data migration

issue_context.title: mysql/mariadb: Database migration failed
issue_context.body:
### The problem

I got the persistent notification about the database upgrade and then received the following.

```
recorder_database_migration
The database migration failed, check [the logs](/config/logs).Database Migration Failed
```

With the following error in the log.

```

Source: components/recorder/util.py:104

First occurred: 10:07:58 (1 occurrences)
Last logged: 10:07:58

Error executing query: (MySQLdb.OperationalError) (1206, 'The total number of locks exceeds the lock table size') [SQL: UPDATE states set last_updated_ts=UNIX_TIMESTAMP(last_updated), last_changed_ts=UNIX_TIMESTAMP(last_changed);] (Background on this error at: https://sqlalche.me/e/14/e3q8
```
